plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and showy rose-like blooms. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a classic winter-flowering garden plant, with thousands of cultivars in single, semi-double, and fully double forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the plant that produces tea, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil used in Japanese cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant blossoms on bare branches in the cold of late winter, often before the leaves appear. It is a symbol of perseverance and hope in East Asian culture and is highly valued in gardens and bonsai.
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across Japan, Korea, and China, with famous plum groves in Mito and Kyoto
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms bloom weeks before cherry blossoms, and the fruit is pickled to make umeboshi or steeped in liquor to make umeshu.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A hardy evergreen perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers and bright yellow stamens. It blooms in cold weather and often pushes up through snow, bringing color to winter woodlands and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountainous woodlands of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas Rose is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, up to 30 cm across, made of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late summer (peak from late summer to early autumn, with blooms often continuing into February in some regions)
plants.location: Native to the southwestern and southern Cape of South Africa; it is the national flower of South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is among the oldest flowering plants on Earth, and its thick underground lignotuber lets it resprout after wildfires.
